communications.subject: Colorado Open Records Act Request: Alphonsus Follow up (CO)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Colorado Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Thank you for the records your office released on October 7, 2026 in response to my earlier request (REQ-2026-942). I am writing with a separate, narrow request arising from them.

Under the Colorado Criminal Justice Records Act, C.R.S. §§ 24-72-301 et seq., I request access to and copies of the following:

The two telephone recordings described in the released briefing document "LCSO Impersonator Scam (as of 03/12/19)," prepared by Investigator Stephen Gates #08002. The document states that the Georgia Department of Corrections provided Investigator Gates with "2 phone recordings as evidence, during which he could hear what appeared to be scam calls being made in the background." The recordings were received in or about mid-2018 from GDC Special Agent Thomas Bisdorf and appear to be held as digital evidence in connection with your office's investigation of telephone impersonation fraud, including case 2017-9388. That case appears to be closed, based on these documents. 

Format. I request the recordings as electronic copies in their native format (or any common audio format). 

Redaction. I am not seeking the identities of any victims or private individuals. If a portion of either recording would disclose a crime victim's identity or other protected information, I ask that you redact that portion and release the remainder rather than withhold the recording entirely.

Why release is appropriate. I understand that release of criminal justice records other than records of official action is within your discretion, and that the Act defines criminal justice records to include recordings (C.R.S. § 24-72-302(4)). In exercising that discretion, I ask you to weigh the following:

- The recordings document a matter of substantial public interest: telephone fraud run from inside a Georgia state prison against Larimer County residents, which your office investigated beginning in 2017 and which your own records describe as affecting hundreds of local residents.
- Any local investigation is long concluded. Your office's records indicate that full-time investigation ended in 2018. The matter was later referred to federal authorities, and the related federal prosecution in the Middle District of Georgia produced convictions in January 2026.- 
- The recordings contain no Larimer County victim's account. As described, they are recordings of activity inside a Georgia prison.
- Your office has already released the briefing document that describes them.

I request a fee waiver on public-interest grounds. If fees will be charged, please send an estimate before incurring them. 

Thank you for your help.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Dhruv Mehrotra

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Gang Unit Policies & Database Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

1. Policies and General Orders: All current department policies, general orders, standard operating procedures (SOPs), special orders, training manuals, or memoranda governing the Joliet Police Department's identification, documentation, tracking, and validation of individuals as suspected gang members, associates, or affiliates.
2. Criteria Guidelines: Any documents detailing the explicit threshold criteria used by JPD officers or specialized units (e.g., Gang Unit, Special Operations Group) to determine whether an individual is entered into a gang database or designated as gang-affiliated (including criteria regarding tattoos, clothing, associates, social media, or self-admission).
3. Database Specifications: Records detailing the name, architecture, vendor, and system parameters of any local database, software platform, or intelligence system utilized by JPD to store gang affiliation data.
4. Data Sharing & Interoperability: All agreements, memorandums of understanding (MOUs), or policy documents detailing how JPD shares or receives gang-related data with outside entities (e.g., county sheriff's offices, Illinois State Police, federal agencies, or regional multi-jurisdictional intelligence centers).
5. Auditing, Oversight, and Removal: Any policies, guidelines, or logs concerning the periodic review, auditing, purging, or removal of individuals' names from JPD or shared gang databases, including any provisions allowing individuals to contest or appeal their designation.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

M
